title: Create Buttonhole
content: ### Objective Create buttonholes and place them as desired. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Buttonhole 3D Toolbar ▶ Buttonhole ### Operation #### Create Buttonhole 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Buttonhole 3D Toolbar ▶ Buttonhole 2. Click on a desired point on the 3D Garment or 2D Pattern. → A buttonhole is created. 3. Enter the number of garment layers and click OK. → The buttonholes are now being created. #### Input Measurement for Buttonhole Position 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Buttonhole 3D Toolbar ▶ Buttonhole 2. Right-click on the 2D pattern where buttonholes would be placed. → The Moving Distance window appears. 3. Input desired measurements for accurate placement. → Placement preview depending on the input value displays along the mouse in the 2D window. 4. Click OK to place. → The buttonholes are now being created.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for creating and positioning buttonholes on 3D garments and 2D patterns using the Buttonhole 3D Toolbar.

title: Tack
content: ### Objective Use this function to visualize fit adjustments by tacking temporarily. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Tack ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Tack 2. Click on an initial point on a draped Garment. → A point is now being created with a dotted line following. 3. Click on an endpoint. → Another point is now being created with a yellow highlighted line. → Same tack is now being created in the 2D Pattern. 4. Activate Simulate. → The Garment is now being simulated while the two points are being fixed to each other. ※ Note: It is also available to create and modify tacks in the 2D window (ver3.1.0). ###
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to visualize fit adjustments in garment design through the Tack function, allowing users to create and simulate tacks in both 3D and 2D views.

title: Piping Property Setting
content: ### Objective Modify the physical Piping properties at Property Editor. ### Location Property Editor ### Explanation Piping properties appear in the Property Editor when a Piping is selected with the Select/Move tool or the Edit Piping tool. Information | Name | Renames selected Piping. ---|---|--- Line Length | Displays the line length of selected Piping. Dimension | Width (mm) | Adjusts the width of selected Piping between the value of 1~15mm. Particle Distance (mm) | Adjusts the Particle Distance of selected Piping between the value of 1~5mm. Finishing | Start | Close start of piping End | Close end of piping | Fabric | Applies fabric settings to selected Piping from the drop-down item list of Fabric. Piping's fabric texture can be edited using the edit_texture.png Edit Texture tool (ver4.2.0). Hide | Shows/hides selected Piping. (Select a Piping from the Scene tab in the Object Browser to reveal menu.)
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on modifying the physical properties of piping in the Property Editor, including renaming, adjusting dimensions, and applying fabric settings.

title: Play Motion
content: ### Objective Play Pose(*.pos) or Motion(*.mtn) files. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Play Motion 2D Toolbar ▶ Play Motion ### Operation #### Pose 1. Open a Pose file. → When a Pose file is loaded, the Play Motion tool is automatically activated. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Play Motion 2D Toolbar ▶ Play Motion 3. Click the Play Motion tool while the Avatar changes pose. → The Avatar stops temporarily. → The Avatar changes pose again. #### Motion 1. Open a Motion file. → The Play Motion tool now can be selected. 2. Click the Play Motion tool. → The motion is played. * The Transition Animation for the default avatars of the version 10 is not compatible with the previous versions.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for playing Pose and Motion files using the Play Motion tool in the Avatar interface.

title: Edit Texture Size (Property Editor)
content: ### Objective Use the Property Editor to resize the texture applied to the Patterns. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric (Select the Desired One) ▶ Property Editor ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric (Select the Desired One) ▶ Property Editor → The selected Fabric's properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Find the Transformation option which only appears when a texture is applied to a Pattern. Option | Description ---|--- Angle | Type in the rotating angle. Width | Set the texture width. Height | Set the texture height. Lock Aspect Ratio | Lock the width and height ratio.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Property Editor to resize textures applied to Patterns in the Fabric Tab of the Object Browser.

title: Reset Topstitch Style Property
content: ### Objective Reset Topstitch style properties to default values (ver2.5.0). ### Location Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Right-Click Topstitch Style Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reset ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Right-Click Topstitch Style Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reset → The Topstitch style properties are now being reset back to default value.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for resetting Topstitch style properties to their default values in version 2.5.0.

title: 3D M:N Free Sewing (VER4.2.0)
content: ### Objective In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns (M) to multiple Patterns (N) at once. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ M:N Free Sewing ※ Note: Hold down the Free Sewing tool for a while to access the M:N Free Sewing Tool. ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ M:N Free Sewing → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Establish Free Sewing Lines on multiple Patterns, which are considered as M Patterns. 3. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. 4. While being mindful of Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on Patterns which are sewn to M Patterns. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M:N Sewing Lines. → All Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. ※ Note: * While establishing the Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * While establishing M:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the Sewing Line cannot be applied. ※ Note: 3D Sewing Video
content_description: This web page provides guidance on using the M:N Free Sewing tool to create and manage Sewing Lines for multiple patterns in a 3D environment.

title: TOPSTITCH STYLE PROPERTIES: Topstitch Face Setting
content: ### Objective Select the face of Topstitch. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ Face ### Explanation ![topstitchFront.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438783711769) | Topstitch is only set for the front of the Fabric. ---|--- ![topstitchBack.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438783876377) | Topstitch is only set for the back of the Fabric. ![topstitchBoth.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438812482457) | Topstitch is set for the both sides of the Fabric. ※Note: Topstitch placed on the back of the Fabric do not appear in the 2D window (ver4.2.0).

content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adjusting the interval between Topstitches on Internal Lines or Pattern outlines using the Topstitch Property Editor.

title: Merge Points on Internal Lines
content: ### Objective Join or merge two open points on Internal Lines. ※ Note: When a point on the Internal Line is open, it is hollow, whereas when a point on the Internal Line is closed, it is filled. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern ### Operation #### Join Overlapping Points 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Select overlapping points and right click to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Join Overlapping Points. → Two overlapping points are joined and closed. #### Merge to Point 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Select two points on Internal Lines to be merged. 3. Right click on the point which the other point should be merged to. When the pop-up menu appears, select Merge to Point. → The point is merged to the right-clicked point. #### Merge to Average 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Select two points on the Internal Lines to be merged. Then, right click on either point to access the pop-up menu and select Merge to Average. → The selected points are merged to their average point. #### Intersect & Merge 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Select two points to be merged. 3. Right click on the points to access the pop-up menu and select Intersect & Merge. → The selected points are shortened or extended maintaining their current slope and are merged where they intersect.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for joining or merging open points on Internal Lines in 2D patterns using various methods.

title: Zoom In/Out, Rotation
content: ### Objective In Marvelous Designer, the mouse wheel and the right button can be used to zoom in, zoom out, and rotate the screen. The Maya and 3Ds Max view control methods are also supported alongside the default view control method and interface can be modified as needed and use differently. ### Operation #### Move Hold down the mouse wheel and drag to move the screen. If you are using Mac's Magic Mouse, please hold down the Alt key on the keyboard and click-and-drag the left mouse key. #### Zoom In/Out Scroll down (zoom in) and up (zoom out) the mouse wheel to zoom in and zoom out the screen. Or, hold down Alt Key on the keyboard and the left button of the mouse simultaneously and drag up (zoom out) or down (zoom in). ※ Note: Zoom in or zoom out using the + (zoom in) and - (zoom out) keys on the keyboard (ver2.4.0.) #### Rotate Hold down the right button of the mouse and drag to rotate the 3D window.
content_description: This webpage provides essential controls for navigating the 3D interface in Marvelous Designer, including zooming, moving, and rotating the view using various input methods.

title: TOPSTITCH PROPERTIES: Flip Topstitch
content: ### Objective Use the Flip function to set a Topstitch on an Internal Shape/Line in a different direction (inside and outside). When setting the Topstitch on the Pattern's cutting line, the Topstitches always appear on the inside of a Garment and the Flip function gets deactivated. ### Location Property Editor ▶ Placement ▶Flip ### Operation 1. Select a Topstitch with Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D window for changing its properties. → Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Placement ▶Flip → The Topstitch direction will now be changed.
content_description: This webpage provides a concise guide on using the Flip function in the Property Editor to adjust the direction of Topstitches on internal shapes or lines in garment patterns.

title: [Property] Scale Avatars
content: ### Objective Scale an OBJ imported as an Avatar. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ### Operation 1. Import an .OBJ as an Avatar. (ver. 10) Import a .FBX as an Avatar. (ver. 2024.0) 2. Select the tool/ menu indicated in Location. 3. Select the Avatar and click the Scale button to resize the Avatar. → The scale Gizmo appears. 4. Click and drag the Gizmo's X-axis (red), Y-axis (yellow-green), Z-axis (blue) or the rectangle. → The Avatar size is adjusted according to the selected direction. 5. Click the Scale button to complete scaling. → The Gizmo is changed to a standard one that is used to move or rotate the Avatar. ※ Note: Scale with specific values in the Property Window after selecting the Avatar.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for scaling an imported OBJ or FBX file as an Avatar in a 3D garment design software.

title: Add Bounding Voulme
content: ### Objective Add a Bounding Volume to add arrangement points. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Bounding Volume ▶ Add ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Bounding Volume ▶ Add → A new Bounding Volume called "Pan" is now being created at the bottom of the Bounding Volume list, and its properties appear in the Property Editor. 2\. Set details for Bounding Volume. Board | Check the list of currently added layouts and edit the properties of the layout by selecting the desired item. ---|--- Name | Changes the name of the Bounding Volume. Arrangement BV | Joint Name 0 | Set the position of the joint(X-ray joint point) where the Bounding Volume starts. Joint Name 1 | Set the position of the joint(X-ray joint point) where the Bounding Volume ends. Shape (ver MD10) | Depending on the shape of the Avatar, the Bounding Volume is set to the Cylinder and Cuboid. Height | Sets the height of the Bounding Volume. Length X | Adjusts the circumference of the left and right radii of the Bounding Volume. Length Y | Adjusts the circumference of the top and bottom radii of the Bounding Volume. Round Corner (ver MD10) | ※ It is active only when the Bounding Volume type is set to Cuboid. Adjust the radius of each corner. Hands/Feet | If this option is activated, the length of the Bounding Volume is adjusted to the avatar's hands and feet. The moment you click that option, the entire Bounding Volume is refreshed. ※ Note: If the order below/above the joint points is reversed, the left and right sides are flipped when arranging the Pattern.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adding and configuring a Bounding Volume in the Avatar Editor to customize arrangement points for enhanced avatar design.

title: Garment Fit Maps
content: ### Objective Utilize four Garment Fit Maps in the 3D window to check 3D Gament's fit. ### Location 3D Window ▶ Hover the Mouse Over the 5th Icon ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window ▶ Hover the Mouse Over the 5th Icon → Four Garment Fit Maps appear. 2. Refer to the table below and select the desired view icon. Icon | Description ---|--- Stress Map (Below ver. 12) | External stress causing garment distortion per area of the fabric appears in the range of color and numbers. Stress Map appears in a total of eight colors: Red indicates the strongest stress (100kPa) while blue indicates zero distortion (0.00kPa). Other numbers in between are expressed as gradation of two colors. Strain Map | Garment's distortion rate due to external stress appears in percentage. Stain Map appears in a total of eight colors: Red indicates a 120% of distortion rate while blue indicates 100% (no distortion). Numbers in between are expressed as gradation of two colors. Fit Map (Below ver. 12) | Fip Map shows the tightness of the 3D Garment. Can't Wear appears in red indicating not wearable area. Very Tight appears in orange indicating a very tight area. Tight appears in yellow indicating a slightly tight area. Show Pressure Points | Show or hide contact points between 3D Garment and Avatar. → Based on the selected icon, Stress Map, Strain Map, Fit Map, or Pressure Points appear on the 3D Garment.
content_description: Explore the 3D Garment Fit Maps to assess and visualize garment fit through interactive stress, strain, and pressure point analysis.

title: Trace
content: ### ### ### ### ### ### Objective Use the Trace function to convert lines/shapes/area to Patterns. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Trace 2D Toolbar ▶ Trace ### Operation #### Trace as a Pattern 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Trace 2D Toolbar ▶ Trace 2. Select the Baselines to be traced. 3. Right click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. →The right click pop-up menu appears. 4. Select Trace as a Pattern. →The selected Baselines are traced as a Pattern. #### Trace as an Internal Shape 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Trace 2D Toolbar ▶ Trace 2. Select the Baselines to be traced. 3. Right click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. →The right click pop-up menu appears. 4. Select Trace as an Internal Shape. →When the selected lines are intersected, the intersection is joined and the lines are traced as one shape. #### Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Trace 2D Toolbar ▶ Trace 2. Select the Baselines to be traced. 3. Right click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. →The right click pop-up menu appears. 4. Select Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes. →The selected lines will be traced as they are. ※ Note: * To easily select a closed shape, double click on the Internal Line. * Click and drag to select multiple Internal Lines at once. All Internal Lines within the marquee box are selected.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for using the Trace function to convert lines, shapes, and areas into patterns within a 2D design environment.

title: How to Fix the Error using Intel Graphics Card
content: ### Objective Learn how to resolve launching error using Intel HD Graphics. ### Operation Since this crashing is due to a Graphic driver which is automatically updated by Microsoft Windows, please re-install the Intel graphics driver after deactivating "Windows Automatic Updates". ### Case 1 1\. Please input "gpedit.msc" on Search tool and execute it. 2\. Local Group Policy Editor ▶ Computer Configuration ▶ Administrative Templates ▶ Windows Components ▶ Windows Updates ▶ activate "Do not include drivers with Windows Update" ![0.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438341413785)※ Note: The option may not appear in the Window versions below. In this case, External Graphics card should be used. (Please refer to [Computer Specification](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358219834649)) Windows 7 Home Edition / Windows 10 Home Edition 3\. Device Manager ▶ Display Adapters ▶ Intel(R) HD Graphic ▶ Uninstall the device and driver software ▶ Reboot Windows ![1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438341588761) 4\. Enter [Intel Support Page](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/intel-driver-support-assistant.html) and download and install the program of Intel® Driver & Support Assistant. 5\. Start scanning the driver. 6\. Download and Reinstall the driver of Intel(R) HD Graphics. 7\. Verify the "23.20.16.4901" version is installed correctly.![2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438420736281) 8\. Please reboot Windows. 9\. If the Error is not resolved with Case 1, please proceed Case 2 below. ### Case 2 If the Error is not resolved with Case 1, please proceed Case 2. 1\. Please enter [Intel® Graphics Driver for Windows*](https://downloadcenter.intel.com/download/30196/Intel-Graphics-Driver-for-Windows-15-40-) and Download & Install the driver. 2\. Approve overwrite to the previous version during Installation. ![3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438420990617)
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions to troubleshoot and resolve launching errors caused by Intel HD Graphics driver issues on Windows systems.

title: I got an email titled "Update Required: Your account is on hold." What does it mean?
content: # **New License Status Policy Announcement: License Suspension After Payment Failure** **Q. I got an email titled "Update Required: Your account is on hold." What does it mean?** **A:** You received this email because your payment attempt during the checkout process failed. This can happen due to reasons such as: * Insufficient funds * Expired credit card * Declined transaction As a result, your license was not activated, and the system has automatically suspended your license status until a successful payment is completed. ⏳ A 7-day grace period is provided, during which the system will attempt two automatic retries to process the payment. * The first retry will occur 3 days later, and the second retry will take place on the final day of the suspension period. If either payments fails, your subscription will be automatically canceled. * * * ## ## **How to Reactivate Your License** 1. Go to “[ _**My Account > License**_](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/mypage/license)” and update your payment method if you wish to continue your subscription. 2. If at least one of the two retry attempts succeeds, the subscription will be reinstated. 3. If you wish to cancel your subscription, a Cancel button is available in the “[ _**My Account > License**_](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/mypage/license) _**”**_ section. ## **Additional Notes** Only personal monthly licenses (recurring payment including trial license) are eligible for suspension and reactivation. This policy does not apply to: * Personal 1 Year Licenses * Enterprise Licenses * Student Licenses
content_description: This web page informs users about the new License Status Policy regarding automatic suspension due to payment failures and outlines the steps for reactivation.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Physical Property Detail Setting
content: Adjust each item of the detailed settings to express Physical Properties not included in Presets. Each property mutually affects one another and a Garment's physical property is expressed by combination of all detailed property values. ※ Note: * The property details are adjustable with the scroll bar or by entering in actual measurement values. * Scroll Bar [0~99]: This is better input method when the constant value is far too enormous. To reduce this inconvenience, the most commonly used Physical Property is split into 99 stages. * Constant Value [0~1000000000] This is better input method when setting far more accurate Physical Properties than the scroll bar method above.
content_description: This web page allows users to customize and fine-tune the physical properties of garments by adjusting detailed settings, enabling precise control over how each property interacts and influences the overall design.

title: Segment Topstitch
content: ### Objective Create a Segment Topstitch (Patterns or Internal Shapes that are split by points). ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Segment Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Segment Topstitch ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Segment Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Segment Topstitch 2. Click on a segment to create a Topstitch. → The Segment Topstitch is created on the selected segment with being highlighted. ※ Note: * Click-and-drag in the 2D window to encompass all segments where Topstitches to be applied. Topstitches appear on all selected segments (ver3.2.0). * Use lasso selection to select Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines where Topstitches should be created on (ver3.2.0). * OBJ Topstitches temporarily disappear when the Simulation is activated, but they appear again when the Simulation is deactivated (ver3.2.0).
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating Segment Topstitches on selected patterns or internal shapes using the 2D Toolbar in the software.
